thesis: Block, Inc. (NYSE: **XYZ**, formerly Square) runs two linked financial ecosystems for consumers and small businesses. **[Fact]** **Cash App** is a consumer wallet for peer-to-peer payments, direct deposit, debit card, stock and bitcoin trading, and buy-now-pay-later via Afterpay. **[Fact]** **Square** (seller) provides payment processing, point-of-sale hardware, payroll, banking, and software for merchants. **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated revenue was **$11.5 billion** (up **10%** versus last year) and gross profit was **$10.4 billion**. **[Fact]** The company reports two segments and had **59 million** monthly transacting actives on Cash App at year-end 2025. **[Inference]** Owner cash is real (FY2025 operating cash flow **$2.58 billion**), but a large share of headline revenue is low-margin bitcoin activity that contributes only **2%** of gross profit in Q1 2026.
why_market_wrong: There is **no classic dated mispricing signal** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** The market still debates Block as a fintech growth stock with bitcoin optionality, while reported revenue mixes in pass-through bitcoin volumes that overstate economic earnings power. **[Fact]** Excluding bitcoin ecosystem revenue, Cash App net revenue rose **20%** in FY2025 and **37%** in Q1 2026. **[Inference]** Generalists may overweight bitcoin revenue lines and underweight the shift toward higher-margin Cash App financial services and Square software attach. **[Inference]** Bears may underappreciate Square's **$250 billion+** annualized gross payment volume and improving gross profit trajectory (+**27%** consolidated in Q1 2026). Return here is **normalized owner cash at price**, not a sum-of-the-parts on bitcoin holdings alone.
